topic: turn GitHub bookmarks into practice: three repos, one runnable lesson, one saved result
audience_job: decide, when starting to learn LLMs from GitHub, what to run first and what to write down
experiment_variable: the thread's first post versus its second post
label: LOCAL_RUN

parts:
Most people don’t fail at learning LLMs because of math.

They fail at turning GitHub bookmarks into practice.

A better path:
1. Find 3 credible repos
2. Choose ONE runnable lesson
3. Save the output in your own learning repo

I built a 13-step guide around that workflow.

Your first deliverable shouldn't be a trained 7B model.

Make an `llm-learning-notes` repo: sources, pinned versions, one actual test result, errors, and the next task.

Start with the public Datawhale curriculum: https://datawhalechina.github.io/diy-llm/

source_angles.thesis: The learning failure is turning GitHub bookmarks into practice, not missing mathematics.
source_angles.evidence: The 13-section guide is written and archived internally; the toy attention experiment inside it passed with five unit tests.
source_angles.counterexample: Saving notes and running a one-dimensional causal attention test does not establish competent LLM engineering; it is a start, not mastery.

source_angles.angle: Choosing an appropriate repo by prerequisites
